name: User Information
location: SYSTEM\MountedDevices (document the device's Volume GUID) correlated against each user's NTUSER.DAT\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\MountPoints2 (per-user subkeys, one per mounted volume GUID).
purpose: Identifies which user account(s) were logged on when a specific USB device was connected, by matching the device's Volume GUID between the system-wide MountedDevices key and individual users' per-profile MountPoints2 key.
key_fields: MountedDevices Volume GUID value - system-wide record of a mounted volume's unique identifier
MountPoints2 subkey name - a Volume GUID, present under a specific user's NTUSER.DAT when that user's Explorer process mounted the device
MountPoints2 subkey LastWrite time - approximates when that user's profile last interacted with the mount
normal_baseline: A device's Volume GUID appears in MountPoints2 only under the profile of its expected/known owner, with LastWrite times consistent with that user's documented usage windows.
anomalies: A device's Volume GUID found in the MountPoints2 key of an account other than its expected owner

The same Volume GUID appearing across multiple unrelated user profiles on a shared workstation in a short time span, suggesting the device was passed between users or the workstation was used by multiple people around the same event

A MountedDevices record for a device with no corresponding MountPoints2 entry in any loaded user hive, despite other evidence (usb-device-history, usb-event-logs) indicating the device was used interactively - consistent with a deleted MountPoints2 subkey
MountPoints2 LastWrite time inconsistent with the device's connect/disconnect timestamps recorded elsewhere, suggesting registry tampering or an unloaded/incomplete user hive
anti_forensic_notes: MountPoints2 lives inside each individual user's NTUSER.DAT, so this attribution path disappears entirely if that user's hive is not collected/loaded, or if the specific MountPoints2 subkey is deleted - deletion removes only that user's linkage without affecting the system-wide MountedDevices record, so a GUID with no MountPoints2 match anywhere is itself worth flagging rather than dismissing.
interpretation: A Volume GUID match between MountedDevices and a user's MountPoints2 key indicates that user's profile was logged on (loaded) while that specific device was present on the system - it establishes presence/opportunity, not proof that the user actively interacted with the device's file contents.
